_README: Per-nationality visa deep-dive: China → Korea. Grounded in official channels (Korean embassy/consulates in China, KVAC/VFS, Korea Visa Portal). Fee/processing VOLATILE (factId visa-china-c3). The 2025–2026 group visa-free trial is flagged as time-limited. No invented figures.

hero.credit: Photo: Pmsyyz / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY-SA 4.0

verdict.headline: Yes — Chinese passport holders need a visa for mainland Korea.
verdict.sub: Individual tourists apply for the C-3 tourist visa at a Korean consulate or Korea Visa Application Center. Two big exceptions can let you skip it: Jeju Island, and (at times) approved group tours.

highlights.title: Jeju Island — visa-free up to 30 days
highlights.body: Chinese citizens can visit Jeju without a visa for up to 30 days, on the condition of direct flights to/from Jeju and no transit through mainland Korea.

highlights.title: Group visa-free (time-limited)
highlights.body: A trial let approved tour groups of 3+ enter visa-free for up to 15 days, running Sep 2025–Jun 2026, with the group-visa processing fee waived over the same period. Check whether it has been extended before relying on it.

tldr: For mainland travel, individual tourists need a C-3 tourist visa — apply at a Korean consulate/KVAC for your area.
Fill the form at visa.go.kr (the only official portal), print and sign it.
Bring passport, 3.5×4.5 photo, household registration, 3–6 month bank statement and job proof.
Going only to Jeju? You can enter visa-free for up to 30 days with direct flights.

jurisdiction.title: Step 0 — Apply in your consular district
jurisdiction.intro: China is divided among the Korean Embassy (Beijing) and several consulates-general, each with its own Korea Visa Application Center. Apply at the KVAC for the district where your household registration (hukou) is held.

zones.name: Embassy & major consulates
zones.covers: Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Shenyang, Chengdu, Wuhan, Qingdao, Xi'an districts

jurisdiction.note: Not sure which district covers you? Check by the province on your hukou; the KVAC site lists each district's coverage.

steps.title: The application, step by step (individual C-3)

items.title: Confirm the visa type
items.detail: Individual tourists apply for the C-3 short-term tourist visa.

items.title: Fill the form at visa.go.kr
items.detail: Complete the application form on the Korea Visa Portal — the only official site — then print and sign it.

items.title: Gather your documents
items.detail: Collect the checklist below, including your household registration and financial proof.

items.title: Submit at your KVAC/consulate
items.detail: Apply at the Korea Visa Application Center or consulate for your district.

items.title: Pay the fee
items.detail: Pay the visa fee and service fee. Fees are non-refundable even if refused.

items.title: Track your application
items.detail: Follow the status via the center's channel. Don't buy non-refundable flights before approval.

items.title: Collect your passport
items.detail: Pick up in person or by courier and check the visa details immediately.

documents.title: Document checklist — with where & how to get each
documents.intro: For each item, here is where to obtain it and what it must show.

rows.how: Valid 6+ months with at least 2 blank visa pages.
Complete on the Korea Visa Portal, print, sign.
White background, taken within 6 months, full face.
Copy of your hukou booklet; it helps establish your residence/district.
Stamped statement showing a stable balance sufficient for the trip.
Employed: employment certificate + leave approval. Self-employed: business licence.
Reservations/itinerary are enough — don't pay for a ticket before approval.
Property, vehicle or deposit certificates can strengthen a first-time file.

funds.title: "How much money should I show?"
funds.body: There is no single published minimum. Case officers look for a stable balance and clear ties to China (job, business, family, property). A steady history is more persuasive than a sudden deposit.
tips: Show a stable 3–6 month balance, not a last-minute lump sum.
Add proof of ties: employment, business licence, or property.
First-time traveler? A stronger financial + asset file helps.

items.d: Applying outside the consular district of your hukou. Apply where your household registration is held.
Jeju visa-free is Jeju-only with direct flights — it does not allow mainland travel.
A big lump sum right before applying. Show steady, explainable funds.
Buying non-refundable tickets before approval — a reservation is enough.
The group visa-free trial was time-limited (through Jun 2026). Reconfirm before you count on it.

items.q: Do Chinese citizens need a visa for Korea?
items.a: For mainland Korea, yes — individual tourists apply for a C-3 tourist visa. Jeju Island allows visa-free entry up to 30 days, and approved group tours have had time-limited visa-free windows.
You can enter Jeju without a visa for up to 30 days, but only on direct flights to and from Jeju — you cannot transit through mainland Korea.

items.q: Can tour groups still enter visa-free?
items.a: A trial for approved groups of 3+ ran Sep 2025–Jun 2026. Because such schemes are time-limited, confirm the current status with your travel agency or the embassy.
At the Korea Visa Application Center or Korean consulate for the district where your hukou is registered.

items.q: How much money do I need to show?
items.a: No fixed minimum — show a stable 3–6 month balance plus ties to China. Fees are non-refundable.

items.q: Do I still need the e-Arrival Card?
items.a: Entry-document rules such as the e-Arrival Card can still apply. Check the current rules near your travel date.
